pr_title: net: sockets: tls: Fix TLS/DTLS client POLLHUP notification
pr_body:
The `poll()` function did not report POLLHUP if the peer ended the DTLS
session, making it impossible to detect such event on the application
side.

On the other hand, TLS erroneously reported POLLHUP along with each
POLLIN event, as the 0 returned by the `recv()` socket call was
wrongly interpreted (it was expected to get 0 in return as 0 bytes were
requested).

Fix this by introducing a helper function to process the mbedtls context
and verify if new application data is pending. Use this new function in
the poll handler, instead of a socket `recv()` call, to remove any
ambiguity in the usage, for both TLS and DTLS.

Fixes #37720

Signed-off-by: Robert Lubos <robert.lubos@nordicsemi.no>

issue_context.title: net: dtls: received close_notify alerts are not properly handled by DTLS client sockets
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
In the current state of the DTLS implementation, received `close_notify` alerts are not properly handled by a DTLS client socket.

According to the mbedtls documentation the SSL context must be reset when `mbedtls_ssl_read ` returns the following:

> If this function returns something other than a positive value, MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_WANT_READ, MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_WANT_WRITE, MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_ASYNC_IN_PROGRESS, MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_CRYPTO_IN_PROGRESS or MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_CLIENT_RECONNECT, you must stop using the SSL context for reading or writing, and either free it or call mbedtls_ssl_session_reset() on it before re-using it for a new connection; the current connection must be closed.
see https://tls.mbed.org/api/ssl_8h.html#aa2c29eeb1deaf5ad9f01a7515006ede5

For the case of `MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_PEER_CLOSE_NOTIFY` the SSL context is not reset for DTLS clients: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/zephyr-v2.6.0/subsys/net/lib/sockets/sockets_tls.c#L1808
This may lead to an application still trying to send data over an already closed connection.

Furthermore, it is not possible to detect (in an application) that the session has been closed when using `poll()` because neither `POLLHUP` nor `POLLERR` are set.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. open a DTLS client socket in zephyr
2. establish session with a DTLS server
3. send `close_notify` alert from DTLS server

**Expected behavior**

- Internally in `sockets_tls`, the SSL context should be reset when receiving a `close_notify` alert on a DTLS client socket (similar to how it is already done for DTLS server sockets: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/zephyr-v2.6.0/subsys/net/lib/sockets/sockets_tls.c#L1893).

- Ideally, `POLLHUP` is set as well on the poll FD so an application can decide how to deal with the closed session.

**Impact**
Possibly a lot of packets are sent over a closed connection unnecessarily until e.g. an application decides to renew the DTLS session.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - Zephyr v2.6.0
comments: @phise Thanks for the report. Please have a look at https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/37794 where I proposed a fix for the issue. `poll()` will now report `POLLHUP` when peer closes the connection, a new session will be established on a consecutive send.

review_comments: Not sure if this change is for good. Is an error condition really related to lack of memory? Or is this just keeps assigned unrelated meaning to POSIX error codes (ECONNABORTED means TLS Close Notify received, and then ECONNABORTED can't be used for proper connection-aborted like cases, and for them, now ENOMEM being used?)

The above function would fail if `mbedtls_ssl_session_reset()` fails, `ECONNABORTED` was used incorrectly as from what I've seen the function fails if it's not able to re-allocate resources from the heap, hence `ENOMEM`.

Likewise, I don't think that this change is for good. TLS Close **Notification** is in no way a connection abort, it's normal connection closure by a peer. Other TLS Alerts would ECONNABORTED. So, if you would need to track if CLOSE_NOTIFY was received, you would need to introduce a flag, but not return confusing error from recv().

I can't return 0 for datagram socket as for stream, because that would be ambigous (it's ok to get 0 on datagram recv). And I won't introduce a custom errno value to indicate that server closed the session, IMO it'd be more confusing that using something from the standard errno space (especially that it was recently unified accross standard libraries we support in Zephyr).

`ECONNABORTED` seemed like a good choice to me to indicate that peer closed the session, especially that I changed other uses of this value to avoid ambiguity (as explained in the commit message). Alternatively, an option would be to use `ENOTCONN` to indicate that socket is no longer connected.

> And I won't introduce a custom errno value to indicate that server closed the session, IMO it'd be more confusing that using something from the standard errno space

Yes (it would have been better to go with a separate API in that case).

> Alternatively, an option would be to use ENOTCONN to indicate that socket is no longer connected.

IMHO, that would be a better choice.
